cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the light you give off is simply what you are.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Across the last several times you knew a next step without seeing the whole way, find what stayed the same and write that sameness in one line. Then set it down.
cells.core:
Not showing off. Simply lit. When the way ahead is dark past the next few steps and you still know where your foot goes, your own nature is moving — no need to force clarity or perform certainty to get across what you see. Anyone near can tell shining from working the room, and yours is the first kind, or this balance wouldn't be the one drawn.
The easy mistake from here is assuming those around you see what you see. Mostly they don't. When you're lit and moving, wait half a step before naming the whole way — long enough for whoever is beside you to catch the piece you just caught. Nothing already yours needs proving.
cells.sheetLine: You're lit, and you don't have to prove it.
cells.verb: letting what you actually are come through
cells.place: where the road ahead is dark past the next few steps

cells.tense: You're holding a future that can't be written into yet, and the holding has become the work.
cells.act: leave it undecided a while longer
cells.ask: Let one plan stay undecided for a set stretch — three days or a week. When it tugs at you, hold off choosing for a bit more.
cells.core:
Some of your shine has turned into a spotlight aimed at where you're headed. In your head you're already there — explaining, certain, arriving before the moment itself — and the certainty lands before the next step has shown you what it is. That step is real, but it isn't the whole way, and you're carrying it as though it were. That's the part that leaves others squinting.
Let one decision stay open for a set stretch. Name it to yourself, set it down, and don't pick it up. The tug will return, and it can wait. Something is still forming there, and decided early, you buy certainty with whatever wasn't visible yet.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already behind you, apologizing for the light on your side.
cells.act: point your attention at one thing
cells.ask: Point your attention at what you've already settled and keep it there — when the rechecking starts, put your focus back on the choice itself, not on whether it was right.
cells.core:
There's something you already are, already made, already past — and you're standing in its doorway asking whether you earned it. That's the dimming. Not humility; the light is still yours, you're just holding a hand over it. You remember being further back than this and haven't caught up to where you actually stand. The road that brought you here is finished. You're still holding the ticket.
Let a decision be decided. Say your reasons to yourself once, and then walk as someone who has already chosen — not as someone still checking the choice was permitted. Nothing new is being asked. The decision is already in your hand; the rechecking is what keeps taking the shine.
cells.sheetLine: You're asking permission for something you already chose.

cells.tense: The pen is down and the room is still being written, and you're reading it as conditions.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: When the next new moment comes today, meet it as it arrives — not as the fourth of a pattern. Check what it actually is before you name what it's like.
cells.core:
You're shining and you don't think it's you. Things land well around you and you read them as timing, luck, or somebody else's doing — nothing in your account of the day has your hand in it, which is hard to keep up and easy to miss doing. The light is on. In your version, the light has no author.
Meet the next moment as it comes, without the earlier ones lined up beside it. What's arriving now is not the last thing again. If it looks like one, check the door before greeting it by an old name. The pen is already moving; you're just not signing. You don't have to claim more than that — only stop crediting conditions for what you wrote.
